dmm-2010-devil-01.title: Substitute L = ln x
dmm-2010-devil-01.body:
For real $x>0$ let $L=\ln x$. Then $\ln(x^4)=4L$ and the equation is $16L^2=L^6$, i.e. $L^2(L^4-16)=0$. So $L=0$ or $L^2=\pm4$; for real $L$: $L=0,\pm2$. Hence $x=1,\ e^2,\ e^{-2}$.

**Answer: $x=1,\ e^2,\ e^{-2}$**

dmm-2010-devil-02.title: Information bound and binary search
dmm-2010-devil-02.body:
*Lower bound.* Each attempt gives Yiwen one bit (Alan either reports $M>N$ or he does not). With $k$ attempts she can distinguish at most $2^k$ cases, and there are $2011$ possible starting numbers, so $2^k\ge2011$ forces $k\ge11$.

*Upper bound.* Binary search: send $M=1024$. If Alan says $M>N$, then $N\in[0,1023]$ (at most $1024$ possibilities). Otherwise his number becomes $N-1024\in[0,986]$ (at most $987$ possibilities), and Yiwen remembers the subtracted $1024$. In either case at most $1024=2^{10}$ possibilities remain, and each further attempt (send $M=$ half of the current range size) halves them, so $10$ more attempts suffice. Total $11$.

**Answer: 11**

dmm-2010-devil-03.title: Complement
dmm-2010-devil-03.body:
Numbers with at most $3$ divisors: $1$ (one divisor), the primes (two divisors; there are $15$ primes up to $50$), and squares of primes (three divisors): $4,9,25,49$. That is $1+15+4=20$ numbers, so $50-20=30$ numbers have at least $4$ divisors.

**Answer: 30**

dmm-2010-devil-04.title: Telescoping and Pisano period
dmm-2010-devil-04.body:
$\sum_{i=0}^mF_i=F_{m+2}-1$ (induction, or telescoping $F_i=F_{i+2}-F_{i+1}$). With $m=97!+4$ the sum is $F_{97!+6}-1$. The Fibonacci numbers mod $10$ repeat with period $60$, and $60\mid97!$, so $F_{97!+6}\equiv F_6=8\pmod{10}$ and the sum ends in $8-1=7$.

**Answer: 7**

dmm-2010-devil-05.title: Factor
dmm-2010-devil-05.body:
Let $2p+1=m^3$ with $m$ odd. Then $p=\frac{m^3-1}2=\frac{m-1}2\,(m^2+m+1)$. Since $m^2+m+1>1$, for $p$ to be prime we need $\frac{m-1}2=1$, so $m=3$ and $p=13$ (check: $2\cdot13+1=27$).

**Answer: 13**

dmm-2010-devil-07.title: Center the set
dmm-2010-devil-07.body:
Let the middle (fifth) integer be $k$, so the set is $k-4,\dots,k+4$. The condition is $\sum_{j=-4}^0(k+j)^2=\sum_{j=1}^4(k+j)^2$. The left side is $5k^2-20k+30$ and the right side is $4k^2+20k+30$, so $k^2-40k=0$ and $k=40$ (positive). The sum of the nine integers is $9k=360$.

**Answer: 360**

dmm-2010-devil-08.title: Determine the array
dmm-2010-devil-08.body:
Let $a_{ij}$ be the entry in row $i$, column $j$. Row $1$ is arithmetic with $a_{11}=1$, $a_{13}=\frac12$, so $a_{1j}=\frac{5-j}4$. Column $1$ is geometric with $1,\frac12$, so its ratio is $\frac12$. Column $j$ is geometric with some ratio $r_j$: $a_{ij}=a_{1j}r_j^{\,i-1}$. 

Row $2$ must be arithmetic, so $(5-j)r_j=L(j)$ for a linear function $L$ of $j$. Row $3$ must also be arithmetic, so $(5-j)r_j^2=\frac{L(j)^2}{5-j}$ is linear in $j$ for all integers $j\ne5$; as an identity of rational functions this forces $(5-j)\mid L(j)^2$, hence $L(5)=0$, $L(j)=c(5-j)$ and $r_j=c$ for all $j$: all columns have the same ratio. Since $r_1=\frac12$, every column has ratio $\frac12$: $a_{ij}=\frac{5-j}4\cdot2^{1-i}$.

The diagonal entries are $a_{ii}=\frac{(5-i)}{4}2^{1-i}=(5-i)2^{-i-1}$, and $\sum_{i\ge1}(5-i)2^{-i-1}=5\cdot\frac12-\sum_{i\ge1}i\,2^{-i-1}=\frac52-1=\frac32$ (using $\sum_{i\ge1}i2^{-i}=2$).

**Answer: $\dfrac32$**

dmm-2010-devil-09.title: Cauchy-Schwarz
dmm-2010-devil-09.body:
Put $t=\frac yx\in(0,1)$; the expression is $\frac1t+\frac4{1-t}$. By Cauchy–Schwarz, $\left(\frac1t+\frac4{1-t}\right)\big(t+(1-t)\big)\ge(1+2)^2=9$, so the expression is at least $9$, with equality when $\frac{1}{t^2}=\frac4{(1-t)^2}$, i.e. $t=\frac13$ ($y=\frac x3$).

**Answer: 9**

dmm-2010-devil-13.title: Double-angle product
dmm-2010-devil-13.body:
Use $\sin\theta\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}\cos(2^i\theta)=\frac{\sin(2^n\theta)}{2^n}$ (repeated $\sin2x=2\sin x\cos x$). With $\theta=\frac\pi9$ and $n=9$: $\prod_{i=0}^8\cos\frac{2^i\pi}9=\frac{\sin(512\pi/9)}{512\sin(\pi/9)}$. Now $\frac{512\pi}9=56\pi+\frac{8\pi}9$ and $\sin\frac{8\pi}9=\sin\frac\pi9$, so the product of cosines is $\frac1{512}$ and the product of secants is $512$.

**Answer: 512**
